elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Vendor shall defend and indemnify Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim..." — express defence duty running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "defend and indemnify Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of (a)-(d)".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "Vendor's breach of Applicable Law" — uses the defined term in Section 1.2.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (d): "Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party written notice of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "the indemnifying Party shall have control of the defence and settlement of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: "Customer's only indemnity obligation is to indemnify Vendor against third-party claims arising out of Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of Applicable Law." The word "only" makes the limitation operative.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) of the inserted clause covers third-party allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate IP rights.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: the inserted clause contains no exclusions, which is more favourable to Customer than the permitted carve-out; the condition allowing the exclusion simply does not apply.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion is imposed on Customer, so nothing conflicts with this optional carve-out.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specifications exclusion appears, which is at least as favourable to Customer.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The inserted clause contains no procure/modify/replace remedy obligation; Section 9.3's reference to "the remedies required by Section 20.5" is not answered by any inserted text.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund mechanic appears anywhere in the inserted language.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual-fee super-cap is stated; indemnification obligations remain uncapped Excluded Claims under Section 21.3 (deliberate, and favourable to Customer, but the fallback element is unmet).

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all ten preferred elements are present in operative language — defence and indemnity for Customer and its Affiliates, the four required trigger limbs (IP infringement of Services/Deliverables, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), the notice/control/cooperation procedure, and an express "only" limitation on Customer's reciprocal indemnity.

Fallback level is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace, no refund, no 3x super-cap), but only one level need be complete, and the drafter's reason for not adopting the fallback is sound: a 3x cap would erode the uncapped treatment of indemnification obligations already secured by Section 21.3's Excluded Claims.

Minimal: this is a concise insertion filling a wholly missing clause. The drafter trimmed the model language of extras (no "hold harmless", no damages/costs/attorneys'-fees tail, no survival or at-own-expense boilerplate, no exclusions or caps), retained Sections 9.3, 19.5 and 21.3 verbatim, and added nothing outside the preferred checklist.

Preserves intent: the insertion uses existing defined terms (Applicable Law, Services, Deliverables, Customer Data), does not contradict Section 19.5's no-disclaimer sentence, and leaves Section 21.3's uncapped Excluded Claims treatment intact and now operative rather than hypothetical.

Residual drafting point (not an intent failure, because the defect pre-existed the edit and its repair falls outside the preferred checklist): Section 9.3 still cross-references "the remedies required by Section 20.5", and the inserted article is rendered without numbering or a 20.5 subsection. To close this, number the insertion as Section 20 and either add a 20.5 procure/modify/replace/refund subsection or conform Section 9.3's cross-reference; leaving it as-is risks Vendor arguing Customer's Section 9.3 IP-termination trigger is inoperable.
